knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A wobbling ladder is stopped, moved to a firm flat surface, checked and removed from service if it still wobbles. Continuing (option 0) and standing on the top step (option 2) both create a fall risk.
A single climber at a time, with a partner holding the base, is the rule for work above floor-level reach. Two climbers at once (option 0) and the partner going up (option 2) are not acceptable.
The lesson grants no licence. Option 0 is a false claim; option 2 misstates the purpose of the lesson.

practicalCriteria: Given a step ladder and a ladder, the learner completes a pre-use inspection covering rungs or treads, screws, rivets, bolts, feet and locks, and states whether each may be used; the assessor checks the inspection against the scenario faults.
The learner sets up a step ladder fully open and locked on a firm, flat, clear surface, and the assessor confirms the set-up before any climbing starts.
For a supplied above-reach task, the learner works with a second person at the base, one person on the ladder, and no items carried while climbing; the assessor observes each rule.
The learner records the inspection outcome and the task, using a supplied record sheet.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation record for each practical criterion
Pre-use inspection record from the observed task
Task record showing the two-person method
stopWorkCriteria: Learner climbs a ladder with a loose rung, missing screw, damaged foot or failed lock
Learner sets a step ladder up without being fully open and locked
Learner works above floor-level reach without a second person at the base
Learner carries equipment while climbing or stands on a chair or furniture
